c.tagline: A Roman amphitheatre by the Adriatic and the gateway to Istria's beaches and vineyards.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis are available; Uber and Bolt both operate in Pula and are usually cheaper, especially for the short run to the airport.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number connecting to police, fire and ambulance; 192 reaches police directly and 194 the ambulance.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Only minor pickpocketing risk in peak-summer crowds around the Arena, market and waterfront.

hood_desc: The historic core wrapped around the Roman Arena, the Forum with the Temple of Augustus and the hilltop Kaštel fortress; a compact tangle of squares, cafes and Roman monuments that is the best base for first-time visitors.
A green peninsula ~4 km south of the center packed with the big resort hotels, pools and pebble-and-rock swimming spots; the go-to area for a beach-and-family holiday.
A leafy peninsula neighborhood of family houses, a large campsite, beaches like Galebove stijene and Pula's biggest shopping mall; tranquil yet close to the center.
A lively bayside district around Veruda marina with waterfront restaurants, bars and residential streets just south of downtown; good for dining and nightlife near the water.
A residential hillside suburb between the center and the beaches, quieter and cheaper, with apartments and easy bus links; suits travelers wanting a local, calm base.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout Croatia.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 5:00 AM to 11:00 PM with reduced frequency on Sundays; taxis and ride apps cover late nights.
transit.note: Pula has no tram or metro; the compact old town is walkable and Pulapromet city buses connect the center with the beaches, suburbs and the airport.
transit.pay: Buy tickets from the driver in cash or at kiosks; contactless card payment is accepted on many buses. Uber and Bolt are paid in-app.

bus: Intercity coaches to Rovinj, Rijeka, Zagreb and Trieste from the main bus station
ferry: Seasonal catamarans to Venice, Zadar and the Kvarner islands
Boats to the Brijuni islands from nearby Fažana
train: Limited regional rail via Kanfanar toward Rijeka (with a bus connection)

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus to the main bus station (~15 min, timed to flights)
Taxi to the city center (10-15 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% for good service in restaurants is appreciated but not expected.

places.name: Kantina
places.note: Vaulted cellar dining room; the truffle fuzi is its signature and stays affordable.

places.name: Epulon Food and Wine
places.note: Istrian small plates and truffle pasta paired with local Malvazija by the glass.

places.name: Konoba Bocaporta
places.note: Family konoba doing homemade pasta and truffles without the tourist markup.

food.name: Boskarin beef
food.desc: Slow-braised or grilled meat from the long-horned Istrian ox, a once near-extinct breed now protected and prized for its deep flavour.

places.name: Farabuto
places.note: Unfussy but serious kitchen with an Istrian-Italian menu and good local beef.

places.name: Kantina
places.note: Regularly lists boskarin among its traditional Istrian mains.

places.name: Konoba Bocaporta
places.note: Homely tavern cooking boskarin in long braises with gnocchi or fuzi.

food.name: Manestra
food.desc: Istria's thick bean-and-maize soup simmered with smoked pork, potato and seasonal vegetables; peasant food that locals still eat weekly.

places.name: Konoba Bocaporta
places.note: Traditional konoba menu where manestra appears as a daily-changing soup.

places.name: Kantina
places.note: Good value lunch stop that keeps old Istrian recipes on the card.

places.name: Konoba Primitiva
places.note: Goat-farm tavern with a daily menu built on its own seasonal produce.

food.name: Adriatic fish and shellfish
food.desc: Whole grilled sea bass, scampi in buzara and lesser-known cuts landed that morning in the Kvarner and southern Istrian waters.

places.name: Konoba Batelina
places.note: Fishermen-run tavern famous since Anthony Bourdain filmed there; book well ahead.

places.name: Farabuto

places.name: Konoba Bocaporta
places.note: Simple grilled fish priced by the kilo, chosen from the day's catch.

food.name: Istrian prsut and sheep cheese
food.desc: Air-dried, unsmoked Istrian ham sliced thin with aged sheep cheese, olives and local olive oil; the standard opening course everywhere.

places.name: Epulon Food and Wine
places.note: Istrian tapas format makes it easy to graze across cured meats and cheeses.

places.name: Pula Central Market
places.note: Historic iron-and-glass market hall; buy prsut and cheese direct from producers.

places.name: Kantina
places.note: Reliable cold platter of regional ham, cheese and truffle spreads.

food.name: Fritaja with wild asparagus
food.desc: Soft eggs folded around bitter wild asparagus gathered in the Istrian scrub each spring, sometimes with prsut or truffle shavings.

places.name: Konoba Primitiva
places.note: Farm tavern whose menu changes with whatever is in season that week.

places.name: Konoba Bocaporta
places.note: Puts wild asparagus fritaja on the board through the spring months.

places.name: Pula Central Market
places.note: Foragers sell bundles of wild asparagus on the outdoor stalls in spring.

food.name: Malvazija Istarska
food.desc: Istria's flagship white wine: crisp, faintly bitter-almond and floral, made all around Pula and poured as the local house pour.

places.name: Epulon Food and Wine

places.name: Kantina

places.name: Farabuto

landmarks: Pula Arena
A magnificently preserved first-century Roman amphitheatre by the harbour, one of the world's six largest, still hosting concerts and film festivals.
Arch of the Sergii
An elegant triumphal arch erected around 27 BC by a powerful Roman family, now the ornate gateway into Pula's pedestrian old town.
Temple of Augustus
A remarkably intact Roman temple from the reign of Augustus, its slender Corinthian portico rebuilt after wartime bombing on the ancient forum.
Forum Square
Pula's living room for two millennia, where Roman pavement, the Communal Palace and café terraces share the city's most atmospheric space.
Pula Cathedral
The Cathedral of the Assumption blends Roman foundations, early Christian mosaics and a Venetian bell tower built from amphitheatre stone.
Kaštel (Venetian Fortress)
A star-shaped 17th-century Venetian fortress crowning Pula's central hill, housing the Istrian historical museum and commanding 360-degree harbour views.
Zerostrasse
A cool labyrinth of World War One tunnels bored beneath the old town, now an atmospheric walkway and exhibition space under the fortress.
Lighting Giants
The towering cranes of the Uljanik shipyard, illuminated nightly in shifting colours, a beloved industrial-art spectacle over the harbour.
Cape Kamenjak
A wild protected peninsula south of the city, its limestone coves, dinosaur footprints and cliff-jumping spots ringed by impossibly clear Adriatic water.
Aquarium Pula (Fort Verudela)
A 19th-century Austro-Hungarian sea fort on the Verudela peninsula that now houses tanks of sharks, piranhas, and Adriatic marine life among its stone ramparts.

train.note: Pula's rail line runs north via Kanfanar; the Istrian network is not directly linked to the rest of Croatia, so most journeys need a bus connection at Rijeka.

bus.note: Frequent Flixbus and Croatian coaches run from Pula bus station to Rovinj (~45 min), Rijeka (~2 hrs) and Zagreb (~4.5-5 hrs).

ferry.note: Seasonal Adriatic catamarans (Kapetan Luka / Venezia Lines) link Pula with Venice, Zadar and the Kvarner islands in summer; year-round boats to the Brijuni islands leave from nearby Fažana.

half.name: Brijuni National Park
half.blurb: Island archipelago of Roman ruins, a safari park and Tito's summer retreat, reached by boat from Fažana.

half.name: Rovinj
half.blurb: Istria's most photogenic town with a Venetian old town and St Euphemia's belltower, ~40 min north.

full.name: Motovun & Istrian hilltowns
full.blurb: Truffle-country hilltop villages and vineyards in the green interior of Istria.

full.name: Poreč
full.blurb: Coastal town home to the UNESCO-listed 6th-century Euphrasian Basilica and its mosaics.

full.name: Plitvice Lakes
full.blurb: Croatia's famous terraced turquoise lakes and waterfalls, a long day-trip inland.
